chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
the man and the woman who are found in one quilt — both shall be lashed one hundred, one hundred.

key_terms.جُلِدَا: Dual passive verb: 'both shall be lashed' — indicates prescribed corporal punishment (hadd or ta'zir)
key_terms.لِحَاف: Quilt, blanket — used here as the circumstantial evidence indicating illicit proximity
key_terms.مِائَةً مِائَةً: One hundred, one hundred — repetition indicating 100 lashes each to both parties

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a man and woman found together under a blanket?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) concerning a man and woman found together under a single quilt. The ruling prescribes a hadd (prescribed legal punishment) of one hundred lashes to each. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, physical proximity of unrelated men and women in a context suggestive of illicit intimacy — even without proof of intercourse — warranted a ta'zir (discretionary punishment) or, if established by sufficient evidence, a hadd. The repetition of 'one hundred, one hundred' emphasizes the equality and individuality of the punishment for both parties.
